newsitem.title: PERU: More hostages leave Japanese embassy residence.
newsitem.headline: More hostages leave Japanese embassy residence.

text.p: A large group of hostages held for more than five days walked to freedom from the Japanese embassy residence on Sunday night, shortly after Marxist rebel hostage-takers promised to release 225 captives.
The stream of hostages filed out of the front entrance of the residence shaking hands with a Red Cross official watching at the door.
Dozens of hostages walked out the front door of the fortified compound into the night air under the gaze of hundreds of waiting newsmen, police and firefighters.
The hostages began to board the first of four special buses driven up to the residence for the purpose.

Marxist rebels inside the besieged building said in an earlier statement that they would release 225 hostages as a gesture of good faith before Christmas. The rebels were believed to be holding around 340 hostages before their announcement.
But they also said they would continue their armed struggle and attacked government intransigence.
